advisor.summary: Section 9831(d) lets an employer with fewer than 50 full-time-equivalent employees and no group health plan reimburse individual-market premiums and out-of-pocket medical care without tripping the ACA market reforms — a compliant QSEHRA is, by statute, not a group health plan. The 2026 caps are $6,450 self-only and $13,100 family (Rev. Proc. 2025-32), indexed annually; benefits must be funded entirely by the employer and offered to every eligible employee on the same terms. This is an employee-benefit play: the modeled number is the employer's deduction, and the owner's own family generally cannot participate tax-free — self-employed owners, partners, and >2% S corporation shareholders sit outside the exclusion. Notice 2017-67 remains the operating manual: minimum essential coverage, substantiation, the 90-day notice, and W-2 reporting.
mechanics: The employer funds every reimbursement — no salary reductions — and payments for individual premiums and §213(d) medical care are excluded from employee income under §106(a) and §105(b) when the employee holds minimum essential coverage.
Two eligibility gates under §9831(d): not an applicable large employer (fewer than 50 FTEs), and no group health plan offered to any employee — including group dental or vision unless excepted.

Same-terms rule: every eligible employee receives the same benefit, varied only by age and family size; new hires under 90 days, employees under 25, part-time, and seasonal workers may be excluded by class.

The 2026 caps — $6,450 self-only and $13,100 family under Rev. Proc. 2025-32 — bind per employee per year; the permitted benefit is reported in W-2 Box 12 code FF, and reimbursing above the cap disqualifies the arrangement.
Employee-side coordination: the QSEHRA benefit reduces any §36B premium tax credit through the affordability computation — for subsidized employees the net value can be smaller than it looks.
The engine deducts total reimbursements against the sponsoring business's income; for a Schedule C sponsor the deduction also flows through to reduce SE earnings in the engine's ordinary sequence.

authority.note: The QSEHRA statute: the under-50-FTE and no-group-plan conditions, employer-only funding, the same-terms rule, and the indexed dollar caps.
The comprehensive Q&A: eligibility, substantiation, the minimum-essential-coverage requirement, W-2 reporting, and PTC coordination.
Sets the 2026 indexed caps: $6,450 self-only / $13,100 family.
Exclude the reimbursements from employee income while minimum essential coverage is maintained.
The employer's deduction for the reimbursements — the quantity the model prices.
Coordinates the QSEHRA benefit with the premium tax credit through the affordability computation.
The penalty for missing the 90-day advance notice — $50 per employee, capped annually.
Defines the medical care a QSEHRA may reimburse.

requirements: Fewer than 50 full-time equivalents and no group health plan offered to any employee.
A written plan funded solely by the employer and offered to all eligible employees on the same terms.
The 90-day advance written notice delivered each year — §6652(o) penalties attach to misses.
Proof of minimum essential coverage before any reimbursement, plus expense substantiation.
W-2 Box 12 code FF reporting of the permitted benefit.
risks: The structural failure mode dominates: offering any group health plan — even one inherited in an acquisition — or exceeding the indexed caps takes the arrangement outside §9831(d), and a failed QSEHRA becomes an ordinary non-compliant group health plan facing §4980D exposure at $100 per employee per day; Notice 2017-67 is the controlling ruling on where the line sits.
Notice failures draw §6652(o) penalties of $50 per employee, capped annually.
Reimbursements to employees who lack minimum essential coverage are taxable to them.
Owner expectation management belongs in the engagement: the owner's family generally receives no tax-free benefit — the value lies in the deduction and the workforce benefit.
stateNotes: Conformity: federal-AGI states exclude QSEHRA reimbursements from employee income just as federal law does, and the employer deduction follows the federal business-income computation.
PTET: for S corporation and partnership sponsors, the reimbursement deduction shrinks the entity income base a PTET election taxes — order of operations, not a stacked benefit.
Missouri: conforms via RSMo §143.121; a Missouri pass-through electing the RSMo §143.436 PTET computes it after this deduction, while Schedule C sponsors have no PTET interaction.
reviewChecklist: FTE count documented below 50 and no group plan in force (or termination dated before the QSEHRA effective date).
Current-year caps pulled from the applicable Rev. Proc. and written into the plan.
90-day notice delivered, with proof of distribution retained.
Minimum-essential-coverage attestations and substantiation collected before each reimbursement.
W-2 code FF amounts reconcile to the plan records.

client.teaser: Help employees with health costs — no group insurance plan required.
client.headline: A health benefit for small teams, without group insurance
plainEnglish: If your business is small and has no group health plan, this program was made for you. Instead of buying a costly group policy, the business pays each employee back for their own health insurance and medical bills, up to a yearly cap set by the IRS.
The business deducts every dollar. Employees get the money tax-free. You pick the amount, up to the cap, so the cost never surprises you.

One honest note: this program is built for your employees, not for you as the owner. The rules keep most owners from being paid back tax-free. Your win is the deduction and a stronger team, and we pair it with other tools for your own family's health costs.
client.analogy: Instead of buying everyone the same one-size jacket, you hand each employee a tax-free allowance for the coat they already picked.
benefits: Every reimbursement is a business deduction
You set the budget — no group-plan premium spiral
A real hiring edge for a small team
steps: WE confirm you qualify and set reimbursement levels within the caps.
WE prepare the written plan and the required employee notices.
YOU reimburse employees once they show proof of coverage and expenses.
WE handle the deduction and the W-2 reporting at year-end.
clientCommitments: Never reimburse without proof of coverage and a receipt
Send the employee notice on time every year
Tell us if headcount nears 50 or anyone proposes a group plan

annualMaintenance: Update the plan caps to each year's Rev. Proc. figures
Recount FTEs and confirm no group plan has crept in
Audit notice distribution and substantiation records
